To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1), P-peak at the top of the section was reached earlier than at the bottom, (2) the T- peak at the top of section was reached earlier, (3) exhumation was diachronic, (4) the upper crustal section was exhumed earlier than the lower crustal section.
the Variscan lower-crust of Calabria was affected by two distinct metamorphic events, which occurred in a diachronic way, with an earlier and a later phase.
the lower crust of Serre (Calabria) underwent a diachronic and different evolution during the Variscan orogeny.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the reconstruction of the P–T paths of a lower crustal section of Calabria, in order to understand the Variscan evolution of the southern part of the Calabria–Apennines arc.
the tectono-metamorphic history of the lower crust and its evolution from the Variscan orogeny to the exhumation of the lower crustal units.

the reconstruction of the P–T paths and tectonic evolution of a Variscan crust section, which is representative of the southern Calabria lower crust and, in general terms, of the southern European Variscan crust.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the lower crust of Serre underwent a complex tectono- metamorphic evolution, characterized by a diachronous Variscan exumation of the upper and the lower crust, which occurred along different P–T paths.
the lower crust of Serre was thickened by subduction and collision, and then exhumed by erosion and extension, with a diachronic evolution of the two portions.
the lower crust of southern Calabria experienced a complex evolution, characterized by a diachronic tectono- thermal evolution and different metamorphic histories.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the exhumation was faster in the upper portion of the section, where it started 325–330 Ma ago, and slower in the lower portion, where it started later (about 310 Ma) but lasted longer.
the lower crust was exhumed in a diachronic way from the top to the bottom and the lower crust of Serre was exhumed later than that of the northern part of Calabria.
the lower crust of Serre underwent a Variscan evolution with an earlier and more rapid exhumation than that of the upper crust.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, despite of the different metamorphic evolution and the different P–T paths, the two portions of the section have experienced the same tectonic evolution, i.e. crustal thickening, isobaric heating, exhumation and cooling, and the same P–T– t paths, but with different timing.
the Variscan t-t path for the Serre lower crust can be explained by the combined effects of the exhumation and the cooling.
different tectonic processes, including the exhumation of the lower crust, can be described by a single model.
